body:
Hi, I moved the issue to a discussion, as this is technically not a bug but more of a feature request to support Node.js-like methods in the Edge runtime.

Personally, I am not sure we would want to move forward with this as the Edge runtime tries to only use Web APIs, whenever possible.

Let's continue the discussion first here: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/41743
author: balazsorban44

body:
I only added methods that are both in `ServerResponse` and `NextResponse` so there shouldn't be any breaking changes if you decide that GSSP will have a `Response` object in `context.res`

Also, `context.req` already has the Nodejs `IncomingMessage` signature so this PR would not introduce any new behaviour

@ijjk mind share how to set dependencies for the test? for some reason newly added test fails with

```
Can't resolve '@mdx-js/react'
```

while previous mdx test passes with same dependencies requirement.
author: kwonoj
kwonoj

body: It looks like it is passing correctly is CI now, is this still an issue locally?
author: ijjk

body:
> It looks like it is passing correctly is CI now, is this still an issue locally?

No, it passes local and CI both by having correct transitive deps. Q in here https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/41919#issuecomment-1301513552 is how did current test for mdx was passing when there wasn't any `@mdx/react` dep in our pkg.json tree 🤔 

Probably minor I guess? since it's @mdx/react is peerdep to next/mdx and should be installed anyway.
author: kwonoj

body:
I believe that test was working as `providerImportSource` wasn't being leveraged in that specific test suite so never attempted requiring `@mdx-js/react`. 

Compiled can get updated when `node_module` paths shift slightly due to pnpm's resolving

body:
Note: The `createApp()` logic currently still performs project standardization on examples passed via `--example`, i.e. making sure the correct dependencies are configured and so on. In order to not conflict with this, `--example` will still prompt users for JS or TS.

We can disable this, and simply defer to the example configuration, but this would not be what I recommend and would be a breaking change. For this reason, you will see tests aliased as `run([projectName, "--js", "--example"])` to ensure that there are not prompts during tests, since `--js` is a proxy for the original create logic prior to #24655.

body:
No worries at all, thank you for the review and excellent work as always @ijjk. Hope you guys find the testing utils helpful.

For the refactor, I would encourage using this “templates and modes” distinction, and use `program.typescript` and `program.javascript` to set up that config. Easy to mess up using those two opposite booleans as what is basically an enum, someone was smart enough to catch I redundantly checked in a `program.javascript = true; program.javascript = false` statement lol.

body:
**Edit:** Maybe I misread your comment. Were you saying that the version in the upgrade guide is the version needed for the stable api (pages) and that the app/ dir version number is not documented because it's still in beta? If that's the case, you can ignore the rest of this comment.

---

Totally get that app/ dir is still in beta. Not trying to complain, just flagging my confusion in case it can resolve any issues before it goes out of beta.

If I read that link correctly (maybe there's something else lower in the page?) it says v13 requires "14.0.0". But this PR "Update[s the] minimal version for appDir to 16.8.0".

For context I had upgraded to 13.0.0 and it worked on my server which is on v14.18.3, but then I upgraded to 13.0.1 and build started to fail with:

```
> Build error occurred
Error: experimental.appDir requires Node v16.8.0 or later.
    at /home/[...redacted...]/node_modules/next/dist/server/config.js:265:31
```

> [#33128 (comment)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/33128#issuecomment-1009456136)

Thanks for the link! Though I think this example should be maintained as long as it's referenced by the [Next.js custom server docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/custom-server).
author: maxproske

body:
@leerob What do you think we should do with the following JavaScript examples? 

I think they should be maintained and converted to TypeScript, however based on your comment [#33128 (comment)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/33128#issuecomment-1009456136), it sounds like custom servers aren't recommended, and therefore the examples can't be updated. If this is the case, it might make sense to deprecate them in favour of the main `custom-server` example?

- custom-server-actionhero
- custom-server-express
- custom-server-fastify
- custom-server-hapi
- custom-server-koa
- custom-server-polka
author: maxproske

body: I think we can remove them in favor of the custom server example 👍

author: timneutkens

body:
> This is already running type checking, it's fine to add it to the place @ijjk posted 👍

It does have type-checking. However, in order to fully test the change, it will need a failing case and a working case:

```ts
import Link from 'next/link';

// $ExpectError
<Link onClick={(e: string) => {}} />

<Link onClick={(e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {}} />
```
author: SukkaW

body: That's fine to add 👍
author: timneutkens

body:
> That's fine to add 👍

@timneutkens That's exactly what I worry about.

If we leverage the production test for typescript check, in order to test the "failing case" we will have to first run `next build` and deliberately let it fail (due to a typescript error), which is expected. Then we will have to run `next build` again with the "working case". Now we have run `next build` twice, just to check that typescript typing is working. It is slow and has unnecessary overhead.

What I proposed is that we should do type testing in the unit tests (it is fast and has less overhead), which I can bring up in a separate PR (I will have to introduce a new package for this, which goes beyond the scope of this PR).
author: SukkaW

body:
> It is slow and has unnecessary overhead.

It's not too bad and nearly all the tests are integration tests running against real apps, this would ensure it always fails when running `next build` instead of just testing if TypeScript fails.

Commit: 8569d966f08bcd894ca09830807f7c5510045be2

`pnpm testheadless test/e2e/undici-fetch/index.test.ts` 
- undici fetch > undici > global fetch should return true when undici is used

<details>
<summary>Expand output</summary>

  ● undici fetch › undici › global fetch should return true when undici is used

    expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

    Expected: true
    Received: undefined

      67 |         const result = await fetchViaHTTP(next.url, '/api/globalFetch')
      68 |         const data = await result.json()
    > 69 |         expect(data.value).toBe(true)
         |                            ^
      70 |       })
      71 |
      72 |       it('global Headers should return true when undici is used', async () => {

      at Object.<anonymous> (e2e/undici-fetch/index.test.ts:69:28)

</details>


Read more about building and testing Next.js in [contributing.md](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/contributing.md).

body:
@styfle Finally got a chance to start exploring this today. Here's a brief update:

- the unit tests in CI are failing with a "file or directory does not exist, uv_cwd" error
- a bit of googling suggests this is related to the shell/terminal/process forgetting the directory it's working in because of changes made to it (maybe it got renewed)
- interestingly, these same tests _did_ fail locally on my machine with the same error
- however, after I renamed a randomly-selected file inside the directory and ran the tests again, they succeeded
- the tests have been succeeding on my local machine since then, even after reverting the above change

I'm going to tinker around with the test command tomorrow and see how CI reacts. Need a way to check CI behavior. Will have to set up a new PR from this branch cause I can't push commits to this PR directly.

body:
Hey @ijjk and @shuding , as of this canary release and more formally in `13.0.2`, our Serverless functions now exceed the deployable threshold of 50MB in our private repo. Any advice on how to opt out of this behaviour?

I've [filed an issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/42641) with some additional notes. 

What puzzles me is that both `linux-core-x64-musl` and `linux-core-x64-gnu` are being added to the build, where I'd imagine we'd need at most one. This is similar [to this issue reported](https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/3652), but the solve seems to be waiting on an upstream `npm` RFC to land.

Thanks for any advice you could provide!

body:
I had another look at this but the behavior seems correct to me.

To further confirmed asked Claude to verify:

- Non-standard values (e.g., NODE_ENV=staging) → Always warns ✓
- Development mode with production commands (NODE_ENV=development next build) → Warns ✓
- Production mode with dev command (NODE_ENV=production next dev) → Warns ✓
- Correct combinations (dev with development, build with production) → No warning ✓

Thanks for the PR. Will keep it as-is.

body:
Can someone explain me why there is a different interface to read cookies from a NextRequest vs a NextApiRequest? Just a regular page `getServerSideProps` vs a `pages/api` route. 

Looked at the docs but didn’t find anything, I’m sure there are good reasons I just can’t find it. DX is a bit weird.
author: donferi

body: yeah agree the different types for cookies are confusing. the middleware typing declares `request` to be `NextRequest` but in my testing `request instanceof NextRequest` actually returns `false`.

body: For people that want to make use of Next.js 13 `app` directory yes, it took me a while at first to figure out why my Tailwind doesn't work when adapting to new changes. Official Tailwind docs already added it so doesn't hurt to add it here as well.

@SukkaW I have another PR (#42435) to check the same thing during the SWC transform, so all projects will have it no matter if they're using TS or not.

The thing about ESLint rule is, it doesn't have the real-time feedback like TS language server here (that shows error indicator without saving the file). Maybe an extension for the editor can achieve that, but not everyone has it installed. This TS plugin approach works with a clean VS Code installation.

Hi @balazsorban44 & @ijjk ,

Looks like `rimraf` is increasing the build time.
I have built a simple custom module specifically for Next.js codebase build called `rmrec` deployed on npm, checkout `npm i rmrec` .

**About:**
``` 
`rmrec` runs a native command `rd` or `rf` based on OS by creating & running a child process 
to delete a folder recursively.
```

**Bench (Node.js-Profiling):**

| |`rmrec`|`rimraf`|Deleted Folder Size|
| :-------------: | :-------------: |:-------------:|:-------------:|
|**Windows**|~165.21ms| |1.24 GB|
|**Ubuntu** |~247.30ms|~542.65ms|1.24 GB|

**Next.js (Cache Miss or First Build) Build Time:**

| |`rmrec`|`rimraf`|
| :-------------: | :-------------: | :-------------: |
|**Windows**|~3m36.392s|~5m8.151s|

**Machine Details:**

| |Windows|Ubuntu|
|:-------------: | :-------------: |:-------------: |
|**Processor**|`Intel(R) Core(TM) i5`|`Intel(R) Core(TM) i5`|
|**Version:** |`Windows 11 Pro`| `Ubuntu-22.04.1`|
|**Memory:** |`4GB`|`2GB`|
|**Node.js:** |`v18.12.1`|`v18.12.1`|



### Raised PR with new  `rmrec` changes, Please provide feedback if anything can be changed or improved, really appreciate your time.

body:
How about ignoring local `node_modules` folder instead? Copying files over it helps avoid runtime issues, but local `node_modules` still end up in one of the image layers and thus increase total image size.

Hmm it’s there already:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/b1932b081a95bf535d82faef1c4d7d7ca3de2940/examples/with-docker/.dockerignore#L3
author: kachkaev

body:
I'm not totally convinced the `builder` step is even necessary. The [with-docker-compose Dockerfile](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/examples/with-docker-compose/next-app/prod.Dockerfile) gets away without doing a full copy of `node_modules`.

If it is actually an optimization, I'd love to apply the fixed version to the other Docker examples as well.

body: This changed the undocumented way to programmatically preload `LoadableComponent`s from `dynamic`, it is now `LoadableComponent.preload()` rather than `LoadableComponent.render.preload()`.
author: klarstrup
arishoham

body: @arishoham as described the method is still there except it is now on the parent rather than `render`
author: klarstrup

body: As of Next 13.1 it appears that preload method doesn't exist as described above. It doesn't even appear to be an object. Is there a known fix?
author: agusterodin

body:
I see that there is future planned "offscreen" support in React. Will this a solution? 

https://reactjs.org/blog/2022/03/29/react-v18.html

body: It appears that this change that makes it no longer an object occurred on Next 13.0.7. If I console log in 13.0.6, I get an object with preload function as expected. Can you please clear lockfile and pin to latest version of Next to verify?

davidgolden

body: @davidgolden you should use `React.startTransition` for the setState in componentDidMount as the react warning suggested

author: huozhi

body:
> @davidgolden you should use `React.startTransition` for the setState in componentDidMount as the react warning suggested

This fixes it. I also just found that `useLayoutEffect` inside a dynamically loaded component causes the same issue. This feels like a bit of a breaking change that I'm surprised popped up in a minor version.
author: davidgolden

body:
@huozhi We can add `startTransition` to own code but it's problem when we use hooks from some library where setState is called in useEffect/useLayoutEffect :) 

Are there any idea what we can do in this case?

Thanks @timneutkens!

> `next/router` in `app`

I've adjusted the tests for `next/router` to ensure it validates that it throws an error.

> `next/navigation` in `pages`

This will technically not be supported now, with better support coming from using the `next/compat/navigation` hooks instead that have correct `null` typings.

> `next/compat/router` in both `pages` and `app`

Tests have been adjusted to use this compat router for the `pages` and `app` usecases.
author: wyattjoh

body: I wonder if it would be possible to alias these automatically so that you can just import `next/navigation` in either but have the tsconfig for `pages/` be different (`null` in the return type).
author: sebmarkbage

body:
> I wonder if it would be possible to alias these automatically so that you can just import `next/navigation` in either but have the tsconfig for `pages/` be different (`null` in the return type).

The use case here though is pretty specific. The goal eventually is to have everyone switch to using `app/` from `pages/`, but the hooks from `pages/` won't work in `app/`, and the hooks in `app/` won't _completly_ work in `pages/`, hence the distinction here.

`next/navigation` provides guarentees (non-null) for its hooks versus the `next/compat/navigation` hooks which force the user to consider the case where (for example) `pathname` is `null` because the page is prerendering as it does in `pages/`.

I'd expect to see these hooks used in components rather than specific files in `pages/` or `app/` too. If you were to use `next/navigation` in `pages/` today, it will work, until it reaches the condition (like during prerendering) where it would have returned `null`, and instead throws an error.

body:
The `api-routes-apollo-server-and-client` and `api-routes-apollo-server-and-client-auth` are very similar with the only major difference being the inclusion of auth. They both focus on supporting the Apollo Client with SSR and Apollo Client rehydration. On the other hand, the `api-routes-apollo-server`, is a barebones example that only uses Apollo Server and not the client. This is also an example for building static pages. 

Would it be prefered to have a single Apollo Server + Apollo Client example? Based on the content of the examples, maybe only the `api-routes-apollo-server-and-client` and `api-routes-apollo-server-and-client-auth` examples should be merged?

body:
@ijjk 

after 13.04 some our endpoints stopped making client-side navigation and do full page reload.

This changes definitely cause this regression.

This affects urls which have an extension, e.g:

/foo/bar.htm -> before change, only _next data call was made to fetch page props
after change same url triggers full page refresh. 

if experimental.middlewarePrefetch is set to strict, app behaves as before the change. 

Could this be documented, or maybe something was implemented incorrectly?

body: Hey Michael, yes, thanks for clarifying. I have tested both the values `xWidthAvg` and `xAvgLetterFrequency` locally and they both seem to work fine.  In Nextjs' case they have already released the font override changes with the `xAvgLetterFrequency` value, so any change to this is breaking. I wanted to get some through testing done with `xWidthAvg` and then have it released in Next.

body:
I wanted to keep existing dev tests running as-is, and add --turbo tests on top of that. My thought process is:

1. next.js upstream runs existing --dev tests as-is all time
2. turbopack updates enables few tests 
3. next.js upstream now runs those test for --dev / --turbo both

At the time of 3, we expect test will have same changes as current pr (`it.each(dev, turbo)`). Instead of visiting each individual test each time, I wanted to make upfront changes we can easily search codebases for the tests, and the time of 3 only apply small adjustments (`it.each(... [turbo, shouldRun])` -> `it.each(..., [turbo, true])`.
author: kwonoj

body:
@ijjk Simplified PR for the core utility changes first. 

There are some tests need updates if it's snapshot test, since jest will try to invalidate if snapshot invocation differs based on the execution path (--turbo vs. normal). But I can probably update those later, especially it won't block my immediate task to digging turbo repo side test hanging issue. Landing this PR will make things bit easier to bisect issues on my end.

body: Thank you for the feedback @imranbarbhuiya @SukkaW
author: alphaxek

body: Hi @SukkaW @imranbarbhuiya  , how can I fix `(Decrease detected ✓)`
author: alphaxek

body:
@imranbarbhuiya : I see `cross-env` is already in `devDependencies`  in root `package.json` but we need this in below `packages` as well.
1. font
2. react-dev-overlay
3. react-refresh-utils

To have `cross-env` in above packages we again need to add dependency, also I tried to enable `shell-emulator` but it didn't work for me, please let me know if I am missing something or doing something wrong.

@SukkaW I have made `rmrec` open-source and also okay with adding `next.js` team as repo owner to approve any PRs & fix any potential bugs, as long as the solution works `next.js` team can make changes in `rmrec` repo. 


### Please let me know if I can improve anything, thank you so much for your time.

But we added you as the co-author for that PR as you've already have few updates for the fix and tests here in this PR. Thanks for the contribution!

author: ijjk

body: @ijjk I took a look at those tests, but none of them appear to trigger this edge case. I tried adding a new test case that does, but couldn't reproduce this error. Looking at the [`tryApplyUpdates` method](https://github.com/colinking/next.js/blob/ce96595e53a5c47163415cbdcc4bf9c92124f7e5/packages/next/client/dev/error-overlay/hot-dev-client.js#L307), we would need to create a scenario where the compilation's hash changes (so that `isUpdateAvailable` returns `true`) but which does not produce any updated modules according to webpack's `check` method. Any advice on how to do that?
author: colinking

body: I see, if we can narrow in on a test case in a follow-up then that'd be great but don't want to block this on that as it is a tricky case.

Thanks for merging @ijjk! However, your changes reverted part of the fix:

> When `updatedModules` is `null`, we skip the `apply()` call as this was producing `apply() is only allowed in ready status (state: idle)` errors. This matches [the prior behavior when `autoApply` was enabled](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/8241da7f1e75c5581ba535d127fa66aeb9eb2ac8/lib/hmr/HotModuleReplacement.runtime.js#L266-L272).

I get those errors when running with the latest `next@canary`:

```
warn  - Fast Refresh had to perform a full reload. Read more: https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/fast-refresh#how-it-works
Error: apply() is only allowed in ready status (state: idle)
    at https://app.airplane.so:5000/_next/static/chunks/webpack.js?ts=1669127927262:615:21
```

body:
Hey, I have been trying this in my project, most things work but seems like next/link still uses the "trailingSlash" behaviour and doesn't ignore it.

As an example, using `skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true;` and `trailingSlash: true`

`<Link href="/apple/">` --> renders as `<a href="/apple/">`
`<Link href="/apple">` --> renders as `<a href="/apple/">`

 using `skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true;` and `trailingSlash: false`

`<Link href="/apple/">` --> renders as `<a href="/apple">`
`<Link href="/apple">` --> renders as `<a href="/apple">`

I guess we need some changes to make sure next/link ignores it too.
